titulo: Con lo que + indicative = with all the..., given how much...
subtitulo: ¿Vas a salir con lo que llueve?
regla: Con lo que + indicative points to something big that should have stopped or changed the result: ¿Sales con lo que llueve? = in all this rain? Often with surprise: No sé cómo..., Me sorprende que... Followed by a subjunctive or used literally, con lo que just means with what(ever).

bloques.texto: Meaning: _given how much..., with all the..., considering..._ The **con lo que** fact is an obstacle, and the result happens anyway (or is surprising).
Often after **No sé cómo..., Me sorprende que..., No puedo creer que...**
It can also open the sentence as a complaint: **¡Con lo que me costó y ahora no sirve!**
Tip: **con lo que** = _with all that..._ and a raised eyebrow.

lista.es: No sé cómo no estás agotado ==con lo que corres==.
lista.en: I don't know how you're not exhausted, with all the running you do.

lista.es: ¿Vas a salir ==con lo que está lloviendo==?
lista.en: You're going out in all this rain?

lista.es: Me sorprende que esté tan flaco ==con lo que come==.
lista.en: I'm amazed he's so skinny given how much he eats.

lista.es: ¡==Con lo que me costó== este curso, y ahora no lo validan!
lista.en: After all this course cost me, and now they won't recognize it!
With all the studying you did, you'll surely pass.

filas.t: Puedes ayudar con lo que tengas.

lista.nota: With the subjunctive (or a plain sense), it's just _with whatever you have_.
The obstacle is a real fact: indicative.

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _You're tired? With all you slept!_
In Spanish: _I don't know how she's not cold, with all the wind there is._
lista.r: No sé cómo no tiene frío, con lo que sopla el viento.

lista.p: Obstacle or literal? _Haz la sopa con lo que haya en el refri._
